page: Microsoft Azure D4ls_v6 is a low-memory variant of the general-purpose Dlsv6 virtual machine series, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. The instance is allocated 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 260 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction sets such as AVX-512, Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for deep learning acceleration, and cryptographic offloads including AES and SHA-NI. The instance contains no dedicated GPUs and does not bundle local disk storage, relying on external Premium Storage attachment.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded CPU execution contrasted with lower multi-core and memory throughput. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2115.0 and gzip single-threaded compression speeds of 31.28 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Text processing also registers within the upper quartile at 2529.0 points. Conversely, its multi-core stress-ng throughput (3908.06) and clang compilation benchmarks (5185.0) fall into the bottom 25 percent, limited by the 2 physical core count. Memory bandwidth reflects similar constraints, with large-block uncached read speeds of 36.43 GB/sec and write speeds of 25.65 GB/sec, resulting in a PassMark memory score of 1647.88.

Given its low memory footprint relative to its vCPU allocation, the D4ls_v6 serves as a cost-efficient alternative for CPU-dependent tasks that do not require extensive RAM. Workloads such as static web serving (measured at 7.63 GB/sec throughput), basic database queries, lightweight background job workers, microservices, and single-threaded batch processing align well with this hardware profile. Workloads requiring in-memory dataset manipulation, large multi-core build pipelines, or local scratch storage will find the instance limited by its 8.0 GB RAM capacity and lack of local NVMe disks.
description: Microsoft Azure D4ls_v6 is a low-memory general-purpose virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores, 2 threads per core) on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Backed by 8.0 GB of RAM and 260 MB of L3 cache, the system includes vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance lacks local storage disks and discrete GPUs. Benchmark testing reveals strong single-core compute performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2115.0 and rapid gzip compression of 31.28 GB/sec. However, multi-core throughput and memory subsystem benchmarks rank lower due to physical core limits and a 2.0 GB per core memory allocation. The D4ls_v6 is suited for web serving, microservices, lightweight application runtimes, and single-threaded compute tasks where large memory allocations are unnecessary.

bullet_points: 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores operating up to 4.2 GHz
8.0 GB system memory providing a cost-effective 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation
Hardware support for Intel AMX, AVX-512, and cryptographic instruction sets
Strong single-core and text processing benchmark results
No bundled local storage, requiring attached remote network storage
Well suited for static web serving, microservices, and lightweight CPU processing
